about:
P4 calibration set (docs/p4-spec.md section 6): reactions whose reactive
site is known from the literature, with what ALIE is expected to show,
committed BEFORE ALIE is implemented. Run from the repository root:

cases.name: thiocyanate
cases.reaction: kinetic control favours S: kS/kN = 1e2-1e3 in SN2 alkylations and 1e3-1e4 for activation-controlled carbocations; R-NCS forms only under thermodynamic control (isothiocyanates are more stable) or with diffusion-controlled cations (kS/kN 2-10)

sources.ref: Loos, Kobayashi & Mayr (2003) Ambident Reactivity of the Thiocyanate Anion Revisited. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 125, 14126-14132
Mayr, Breugst & Ofial (2011) Farewell to the HSAB Treatment of Ambident Reactivity. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 50, 6470-6505

cases.why: ESP points to N; the 2026-10-22 pilot (prototype ALIE) found its minimum on S (7.10 vs 8.99 eV)

cases.name: enolate
cases.reaction: free enolate: O-alkylation is kinetically favoured (lower intrinsic barrier; Houk & Paddon-Row and Lee et al., reviewed in Mayr 2011 section 3.4.2), C-alkylation is thermodynamically favoured; synthetic C-alkylation reflects metal-enolate aggregates, counterion and solvent

sources.ref: Mayr, Breugst & Ofial (2011) Farewell to the HSAB Treatment of Ambident Reactivity. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 50, 6470-6505

cases.why: no single kinetic site for a free enolate in PCM water; the pilot's ALIE minimum on CH2 (5.71 vs 7.47 eV on O) is a property to report, not a prediction to grade

cases.name: nitrite
cases.reaction: SN2 O/N ratio depends on solvent and reagent: MeOSO2Me + KNO2/18-crown-6 30:70 (EtOH) to 92:8 (THF); MeI 54:46 (DMF, DMSO); NaNO2 + primary/secondary RBr in DMF 55-65 % nitroalkane, 30-33 % nitrite ester; diffusion-controlled carbocations favour O

sources.ref: Tishkov, Schmidhammer, Roth, Riedle & Mayr (2005) Ambident Reactivity of the Nitrite Ion Revisited. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 44, 4623-4626
Kornblum, Smiley, Blackwood & Iffland (1955) The Mechanism of the Reaction of Silver Nitrite with Alkyl Halides. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 77, 6269
Mayr, Breugst & Ofial (2011) Farewell to the HSAB Treatment of Ambident Reactivity. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 50, 6470-6505

cases.why: the selectivity itself moves with conditions, so no descriptor can be graded on one site; the pilot's ALIE tie (O 7.86, N 7.89 eV) is consistent with that

cases.name: toluene
cases.reaction: EAS on toluene: ortho/para directing, activated

sources.ref: Stock & Brown (1963) A Quantitative Treatment of Directive Effects in Aromatic Substitution. Adv. Phys. Org. Chem. 1, 35-154
Sjoberg, Murray, Brinck & Politzer (1990) Average local ionization energies on the molecular surfaces of aromatic systems as guides to chemical reactivity. Can. J. Chem. 68, 1440-1443

cases.why: Sjoberg 1990 Table 1: 11.93 (ortho), 11.96 (para), 12.08 (meta) eV; a narrow gap

cases.name: fluorobenzene
cases.reaction: EAS on fluorobenzene: ortho/para directing, deactivated

sources.ref: Stock & Brown (1963) A Quantitative Treatment of Directive Effects in Aromatic Substitution. Adv. Phys. Org. Chem. 1, 35-154
Sjoberg, Murray, Brinck & Politzer (1990) Average local ionization energies on the molecular surfaces of aromatic systems as guides to chemical reactivity. Can. J. Chem. 68, 1440-1443

cases.why: Sjoberg 1990 Table 1: minima over para (12.31) and ortho (12.44 eV), none over meta

cases.name: nitrobenzene
cases.reaction: EAS on nitrobenzene: meta directing, strongly deactivated

sources.ref: Stock & Brown (1963) A Quantitative Treatment of Directive Effects in Aromatic Substitution. Adv. Phys. Org. Chem. 1, 35-154
Sjoberg, Murray, Brinck & Politzer (1990) Average local ionization energies on the molecular surfaces of aromatic systems as guides to chemical reactivity. Can. J. Chem. 68, 1440-1443
Murray, Brinck & Politzer (1992) Applications of calculated local surface ionization energies to chemical reactivity. J. Mol. Struct. THEOCHEM 255, 271-281

cases.why: Sjoberg 1990 Table 1 and Murray 1992 Fig. 1: minima over meta (13.03, 13.04 eV)

cases.name: anisole
cases.reaction: EAS on anisole: ortho/para directing, activated

sources.ref: Stock & Brown (1963) A Quantitative Treatment of Directive Effects in Aromatic Substitution. Adv. Phys. Org. Chem. 1, 35-154

cases.why: not in Sjoberg 1990; the experimental o/p preference is the expectation

cases.name: chlorobenzene
cases.reaction: EAS on chlorobenzene: ortho/para directing, deactivated

sources.ref: Stock & Brown (1963) A Quantitative Treatment of Directive Effects in Aromatic Substitution. Adv. Phys. Org. Chem. 1, 35-154

cases.why: not in Sjoberg 1990 (fluorobenzene is); the experimental o/p preference is the expectation

cases.name: phenoxide
cases.geometry_source: RDKit ETKDG + MMFF94s, seed 0xC0FFEE (an anion: MMFF is a known weak point, see CLAUDE.md)
cases.reaction: allyl/benzyl halides: O only in DMF, THF, MeOH, EtOH, glymes, dioxane and toluene; in water 49:41 (allyl chloride) and 65:24 (benzyl chloride) O:C, in phenol 22:78; C-alkylation is attributed to hydrogen bonding at O

sources.ref: Kornblum, Berrigan & le Noble (1963) Solvation as a Factor in the Alkylation of Ambident Anions. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 85, 1141-1147

cases.why: the solvent decides through specific hydrogen bonds, which a PCM continuum does not represent; no ground-state number should be read as the answer
